newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt pares gains, while still riding high.
newsitem.headline: German debt pares gains, while still riding high.

text.p: German debt pared some of its session gains as a charge across the 103 level proved untenable even as the mark clawed back some ground against the dollar, dampening fears on rate moves.

By 1432 GMT the September Bund futures contract traded at 102.98 up 14 basis points and just above the session's low of 102.90. Earlier this morning the contract had moved swiftly higher reaching the session high of 103.14, as sentiment was boosted by the slightly firmer mark.
Investors had worried that the downward spiralling mark might prompt the Bundesbank to raise interest rates soon.

On the other hand economists had always stressed the Bundesbank would try hard to avoid raising interest rates prematurely as an end to Germany's five year easing cycle could trample the nation's fragile economic recovery.
Already this morning technical analysts said 103.15 to 103.17 would be the next region for the contract to target, but admitted that these targets might prove a bit ambitious.
At that point dealers said the market was particularly cautious awaiting the U.S. numbers, and after the numbers came in as expected, there was little incentive to do very much.
"As long as the numbers were in line with expecations, and they were, there was absolutely no reason for any sort of massive reaction on the bond market," said a dealer.

U.S. employment costs rose 0.8 percent in the second quarter, matching expectations. "The numbers were already discounted in the market and so the afternoon was particularly dull," another dealer said.
Several dealers said the market would likely be preparing for a consolidation a higher levels.
